title: Grilled Block Island Sea Bass

items.raw: 4 black sea bass fillets, skin on, 6–7 ounces each (or 2 whole fish, 1½–2 pounds each, cleaned)
3 tablespoons olive oil, plus more for the grates
Zest and juice of 1 lemon, plus wedges to serve
1 tablespoon chopped fresh oregano or thyme
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper

steps.text: Mix the olive oil, lemon zest, garlic, oregano, half the parsley, salt, and pepper. Rub it over the flesh side of the fillets and let sit 15 to 30 minutes — the lemon juice goes on at the end, not now, or it turns the fish mushy.

steps.lead: Get the grill very clean and hot.
steps.text: Heat to medium-high, scrub the grates well, and oil them with a folded paper towel held in tongs. Clean, hot, oiled grates are what keep the skin from sticking.
Lay the fillets skin side down and leave them alone 4 to 5 minutes, until the skin is crisp and releases on its own.
Turn with a wide spatula and cook 1 to 2 minutes, until the fish is opaque and reads 135°F in the thickest part.
Move to a platter, squeeze the lemon juice over, and scatter with the remaining parsley. Serve with lemon wedges.

notes.label: Whole fish
notes.text: score each side 3 times, rub with the marinade inside and out, and grill over medium heat 6 to 8 minutes per side, until the flesh pulls from the bone.

notes.label: Fish basket
notes.text: if fish always sticks on your grill, a hinged fish basket solves it.

notes.label: Buy it fresh
notes.text: black sea bass should have clear eyes, firm flesh, and smell of the ocean, not fish.
